name: Iran nuclear programme
value: No IAEA access; Iran rejects inspections 14 Nov
summary: Iran said on 14 Nov that normal IAEA inspections will not resume, rejecting Board resolutions as flawed
state: Iran's mission to the UN in Vienna said on 14 Nov that IAEA Board of Governors resolutions on Iran were legally flawed and that normal safeguards inspections cannot resume while its nuclear sites are under attack (Tasnim). An IAEA report circulated on 13 Nov said the agency could not confirm that Iran had not diverted nuclear material. No new strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or evidence of weaponisation was found as of 16 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: This affects the risk of wider conflict in the Gulf; check FCDO travel advice for Iran and neighbouring states.
rubric_hit: Inspector access curtailed, 60% enrichment unverified = Watch

sources.title: Tasnim — Iran slams IAEA Board's flawed resolutions, rejects normal inspections

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
